title: Key Management Service
summary: A cloud key management service is a managed, hardware-backed system for creating, storing, rotating and auditing cryptographic keys, and for performing encryption and decryption without ever exposing the key material to the caller. Applications and services call an API to encrypt or decrypt, and the service enforces authorisation through the same identity and policy machinery as the rest of the platform, so control of a key is a control of the data it protects. Two design patterns dominate practice. Envelope encryption wraps data with a data key, then wraps that data key with a long-lived key that never leaves the service, which allows large objects to be encrypted efficiently while keeping the root secret in hardware. Customer-managed keys add an explicit policy and lifecycle that the customer controls, enabling rotation schedules, automatic rotation, grants, cross-account access and the ability to disable a key and render data unreadable. Security professionals focus on several recurring problems: keys with policies that allow broad principal access, keys shared across environments, disabled or scheduled-for-deletion keys that break services, missing audit trails on decrypt operations, and key material that is replicated into a region an organisation did not intend to use. Because destruction is irreversible, key lifecycle decisions are treated as high-risk change, and separation of duties between those who can use a key and those who can delete it is a standard control.
objectives: You will be able to explain envelope encryption and why data keys are wrapped rather than used directly on large objects.
You will be able to read a key policy and determine which principals can encrypt, decrypt, manage or delete a key.
You will be able to design rotation, cross-account access and separation of duties for customer-managed keys.
You will be able to triage alerts on key policy changes, disabling and scheduled deletion.
You will be able to describe the blast radius when a key is destroyed and how to plan for recovery.
You will be able to verify that audit logging captures key usage and that encrypt and decrypt events are retained.
